item: #318 — every roster fixture body legally learns every move it declares
baseline: tests/probe_roster_learnset_refusals.js on the roster at HEAD b8f7d999, release e368827481f5: RED, 420 distinct refused body/move pairs (item stage 40 over 7 bodies, ability stage 54 over 34, move stage 340 over 10; goodrahisui 325). Re-derived independently by a scratch walk of assign() through the format's TeamValidator: 637 rows, 420 distinct pairs — the same number. 331 of the 424 move-stage rows are the ENTITY UNDER TEST on a body that cannot learn it (the move stage's CLICKER / quietBody); the rest are delivery or aux moves on a thrower that cannot learn them (Dragapult, Weavile, Kangaskhan, Torterra, Torkoal and ability carriers).
the_change: One pass in assign(), after a rule returns its scenario: every body is asked, through the same TeamValidator judge fixtureAudit uses, whether it learns every move it declares (the control click exempt, as the audit exempts it). A refused move that is NOT the entity is swapped for the nearest legal move the SAME body learns that is the same type, category, target, priority and flag profile, drawn from the roster's own boring-delivery definition (deliveryOf). A refused ENTITY, or a move with no such equivalent, swaps the BODY for the bulkiest legal learner of all its declared moves out of the same pool the body came from (moveBodies for the move stage, CANDIDATES/carrierAbility otherwise), preserving its types exactly where possible, its status immunities and its speed order against every other lead. Every swap is written onto the row's note. ROSTER_LEARNSET_UNREPAIRED=1 skips the pass.
